caveat.title: Values marked * are modeled or estimated:
caveat.discharge: Discharge: natural long-term average for 1971–2000 (WaterGAP model). It does not reflect today's dam regulation.
caveat.nonPerennial: Flow regime: GIRES v1.0 predictions (Messager et al., 2021), not observations.
caveat.flooded: Flooded area: mean annual minimum and maximum from satellite data, 1993–2004 (GIEMS-D15).
caveat.regulation: Dam regulation: storage of the reservoirs upstream (GRanD v1.1) as a share of the modeled natural annual flow. Above 100%, they can hold more than a year of flow. Capped at 1,000%.
caveat.source: Data: HydroRIVERS and RiverATLAS v1.0 (Linke et al., 2019).
caveat.more: About these values and their sources

modeled.title: Modeled and estimated values
modeled.intro: Many values in the panels are not measurements. They come from global models and datasets, each for its own period, and are marked with * where they appear:
modeled.regulated: Large dams regulate the Limay and the Neuquén today, so the flow in these rivers can differ a lot from the natural averages shown here.
modeled.derived: The basin outline, the sub-basins and the courses of the named rivers were derived by this project from HydroBASINS and HydroRIVERS. Most names come from IGN, matched to the river network automatically, with a confidence level shown on each stream. They may contain errors.

sources.title: Data sources
sources.intro: Geometry and values come from the sources below. Each is used under its own license.

hydrosheds.usedFor: River network, basin outline and sub-basins.

hydroatlas.usedFor: Values per stream and per basin: discharge, elevation, gradient, flooded area, lake area, population and dam regulation. They come from the datasets cited below.

gires.usedFor: Flow regime of each stream (perennial or non-perennial): model predictions.

ign.usedFor: Names of rivers, streams, lakes and dams; perennial streams that HydroRIVERS lacks; extra lakes; dam positions.
ign.terms: IGN does not take part in, sponsor or endorse this application. Data derived from IGN layers is shared free of charge.

osm.usedFor: Cities, towns and villages; evidence for river names.
osm.terms: OpenStreetMap data is available under the Open Database License.
